symbols.name: radix
symbols.meaning: The number of values a digit can take, $2^b$, which is the base in which each digit is written.
symbols.quote: The radix is $Q_0 = 2^b$, the number of values a digit can take, which is the base in which each digit is written.

symbols.name: output digit
symbols.meaning: The base-$Q_0$ digit of the output at position $t$, with $0 \le d_t < Q_0$.
symbols.quote: The digit $d_t$ is the $t$th base-$Q_0$ digit of the output, so $0 \le d_t < Q_0$.

symbols.name: carry
symbols.meaning: The amount carried into position $t$ from the lower positions.
symbols.quote: The carry $e_t$ is the amount carried into position $t$ from the lower positions.

symbols.name: processed positions
symbols.meaning: The number of low positions already processed, so that the sums run over $t < \tau$.
symbols.quote: Why this keeps the value: in the identity below, $\tau$ counts the low positions already processed, so the sums run over $t < \tau$.

relations.quote: Carry propagation takes its input from [Radix-digit convolution](radix-digit-convolution.md), whose output is the list of integer coefficients $c_0, c_1, \dots$ of the product of the two digit polynomials.
Carry propagation takes its digit width $b = \lceil \log_2 n \rceil$ from the [base-2 logarithm](base-two-logarithm.md) of $n$, the bit length of the inputs.
Carry propagation computes its digit count by the [ceiling function](ceiling-function.md): $m = \lceil n/b \rceil$ is the number of digits in each input.
